questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Training versus validation versus test data” in this lesson?
options: This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.
Choose a metric that matches the task, compute it on the intended split, and inspect representative errors before interpreting one aggregate score.
This topic removes the need to validate inputs or inspect model outputs.
This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
questions.answer_key: Choose a metric that matches the task, compute it on the intended split, and inspect representative errors before interpreting one aggregate score.
questions.explanation: Training versus validation versus test data: Choose a metric that matches the task, compute it on the intended split, and inspect representative errors before interpreting one aggregate score.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Generalization”, what should a learner verify?
options: verify class/target shapes, threshold choices, split independence, and that model selection did not repeatedly use test results.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
questions.answer_key: verify class/target shapes, threshold choices, split independence, and that model selection did not repeatedly use test results.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: verify class/target shapes, threshold choices, split independence, and that model selection did not repeatedly use test results.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “Baseline models”?
options: Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
Do not use the test split to tune a model and then present the same score as an unbiased final test.
questions.answer_key: Do not use the test split to tune a model and then present the same score as an unbiased final test.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not use the test split to tune a model and then present the same score as an unbiased final test.
